cards.explanation: The answer is, “I am not the Christ.” John doesn't hedge. He openly declares it, friends. (John 1:20) Some folks answer a simple question with a ten-minute speech, but John gives it to them straight and plain.

The answer is True. They ask, “Are you the Prophet?” and John answers, “No.” (John 1:21) That's one short word, friends. It's the third thing in a row that John says he is not, after the Christ and Elijah.

John answers with the words of a prophet. He replies “…in the words of Isaiah the prophet…” (John 1:23) A prophet is someone who speaks for God. So John doesn't describe himself with his own words, friends. He uses the words of Isaiah.

The answer is the way for the Lord. The voice calls, “Make straight the way for the Lord.” (John 1:23) That is the message John says he is carrying, bakers. He's not the destination. He's the one shouting that somebody important is on the way.

The answer is baptize. The Pharisees ask, “Why then do you baptize, if you are not the Christ, nor Elijah, nor the Prophet?” (John 1:25) Baptizing is what John is out there doing, friends. They counted up the things he said he's not, and then asked about what he IS doing.

The answer is know. John says, “…among you stands One you do not know.” (John 1:26) He's speaking to the Pharisees, friends, and he says this One is standing among them. Think about that. They don't know Him.

The answer is that He is far greater than John. John says he's not worthy to untie the straps of this One's sandals. (John 1:27) The straps are about as low a job as you could name, friends, and John says even that is above him. I think that tells you how high John sees this One.

The answer is the sin of the world. John says, “Look, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!” (John 1:29) Notice how big that is, bakers. Not one town's sin or one person's, but the sin of the world. And John points straight at Jesus when he says it.

The answer is True. John says, “A man who comes after me has surpassed me because He was before me.” (John 1:30) It sounds like a riddle, friends, since He comes after John yet was before him. John says it plainly, and I'll let the words sit there.

The answer is revealed. John says, “…the reason I came baptizing with water was that He might be revealed to Israel.” (John 1:31) So John's baptizing has a purpose behind it, friends. Revealed means made known, and that's what John says it was for.

The answer is False. John says the Spirit came down and rested. He saw the Spirit “…descending from heaven like a dove and resting on Him.” (John 1:32) Then in verse 33 he mentions the Spirit descending and resting on the man, friends. Nothing about going back up.

The answer is the Holy Spirit. The One who sent John told him the man with the Spirit resting on Him “…is He who will baptize with the Holy Spirit.” (John 1:33) John baptizes with water, and this man baptizes with the Holy Spirit, bakers. Same word, very different gift.
The answer is the Son of God. John says, “I have seen and testified that this is the Son of God.” (John 1:34) He says he saw the sign with his own eyes, friends. Then he testified about it.
